industrial_frontier.quest.p6.turbine.des: The turbine has been familiar since the second epoch: steam pushes the blades, the shaft spins, the coil gives current. Only the scale changes — and the fact that the steam source can no longer simply be switched off.
Rotor length, blade material and coil decide how much energy you take from the same steam. That is an engineering problem with a measurable answer, not decoration.
Here the whole chain of the epoch closes: ore, purification, enrichment, fuel, heat, steam, current.
industrial_frontier.quest.p6.turbine.sub: A familiar machine at a new scale
Before the seventh epoch you had no site worth letting anyone into or keeping anyone out of. Now you do, and clearance becomes a tool of relationships.

Four levels. No clearance: the faction does not know the layout and works the perimeter. Escorted: a representative enters with a guide, respect grows, operations soften. Working: the faction's engineers work on site — faster repairs and new trade positions, but they learn the layout.
A revoked clearance is not hostility in itself. But the faction remembers both what it saw and how it was shown out. Details: /if_late_bases.
Who is let onto the site
Decide which faction gets a working clearance
industrial_frontier.quest.p7.counterinte: By the seventh epoch you own something that cannot simply be taken: a programme. The spaceport and the assembly shop are valuable for what they can repeat, not for what they contain.

So this epoch's operations aim at information, access and precision. Counterintelligence hunts for calculations, routes and the launch schedule; a precision extraction takes one specific unit, not the shop; a clearance dispute costs reputation, not property.
Each has a negotiation window and a recovery path. Publishing the schedule openly removes the interest in advance: a secret is valuable while it is a secret. Full list: /if_late_operations.
What they take is knowledge, not cargo
Decide what part of the programme stays closed
industrial_frontier.quest.p7.deep_path.d: The short path is three tiers of ready-made motor: build it, fuel it, fly. It is entirely sufficient and reaches every planet in the programme.

The deep path is the engine designer: combustion chamber, injector head, turbopump, nozzle. Here an engine is designed, not bought, and 97 sequenced assemblies are hours of work rather than one recipe.
It leads to low Earth orbit and the station: planets belong to the short path, orbit to the deep one. This branch is voluntary. Not opening it is a legitimate decision, not skipped content.
industrial_frontier.quest.p7.domain_link: Graphite, boron, beryllium, zirconium, lithium, lead and uranium sit in tags shared with the civil nuclear industry: an ingot from one domain is accepted by the other's machine with no adapter. The civil cycle stays with one mod, the strategic layer with the other, and neither rewrites the other's physics.

Steel, copper, titanium, tungsten and aluminium come from metallurgy: 107 plate recipes and 51 ingot recipes inside the domain rest on them. In return it gives what metallurgy has not — reprocessing products and reactor isotopes.

The link to the city is the entrance itself: EV electronics means its power and production. The link to space is titanium and tungsten steel: both this domain and a rocket hull are built from them. That is why the two programmes must be planned together.
Why this is not a separate island
Carry one material from the civil cycle into the strategic one
industrial_frontier.quest.p7.emergency.d: Oxygen ran out. The spreader lost power. The volume lost its seal. Each has a cheap warning — a reserve, a backup line, an airlock — and an expensive consequence.
All three share one thing: they cannot be fixed at the moment they happen. They are fixed in advance, at design time, and that is the only difference between a base and a grave.
The fourth scenario is terrestrial: the rocket came back to the wrong place. It is not lethal, but it costs a trip, and it is cured by one line on the chip before launch.
industrial_frontier.quest.p7.emergency.s: Three failures that cost a life
industrial_frontier.quest.p7.emergency.t: Provide a reserve against all three failures before departure
industrial_frontier.quest.p7.first_launc: The destination is written to the chip. The rocket's tier matches the target: the Moon is tier one, Mars, Mercury and Venus tier two, Proxima b tier three. A motor below the requirement is not offset by fuel or by tank count.

The tank is filled by calculation for the target, not "as much as fits": a shortfall shows before launch — the craft states the required and actual volume. Suit and oxygen are complete, the environmental upgrade is fitted.
The return point is saved. Full order: /if_launch_checklist. It does not change: calculation and checks first, ignition after.
Six checks, none of them skippable
Pass all six checks and launch
industrial_frontier.quest.p7.hbm_entry.d: The strategic domain had no entrance at all. Its assembly machine is produced only by an assembly machine, and everything else — press, shredder, chemical plant, centrifuge, reprocessing — is built from it. Of 704 blocks only 145 had any recipe.
Here it gets the first recipe in its history: titanium plates, a coil, a motor, a robot arm and an EV machine hull. That is the seventh epoch and nothing earlier.

Both anvils moved with it — they are the other half of the same entrance, carrying the domain's furnaces, ducts and cables. The remaining 2357 recipes are untouched. Close the entrance and you close the domain.
industrial_frontier.quest.p7.hbm_entry.s: An assembly machine the mod never had
Every epoch so far added an industry. The seventh adds a choice: the strategic programme and the space programme. Both cost titanium, tungsten steel and EV electronics — that is, they compete for the same metallurgy.
Running them in parallel on one line will not work. That is not a restriction but the point of the epoch: until now the bottleneck was technology, now it becomes production capacity.

The chapter splits into two branches. The upper one is the strategic domain: assembly shop, RBMK, reprocessing and whatever makes this epoch different from the sixth. The lower one is space: materials, fuel, spaceport, launch and planets. The order between branches is yours.
industrial_frontier.quest.p7.intro.subti: Two programmes you cannot run at once
industrial_frontier.quest.p7.intro.task: Understand what the two programmes compete for
industrial_frontier.quest.p7.intro.title: The seventh epoch
industrial_frontier.quest.p7.planetary.d: The Moon: bauxite and gravity of 1.63 against Earth's 9.81 — launching from here is cheaper. You pay with no atmosphere at all and 113 kelvin.

Mars is the richest planet of the programme: copper, iron, nickel, zinc, tungstate and rare earths; there is an atmosphere, but no oxygen in it, and the year lasts 687 days. That is a base, not an excursion. Mercury gives mercury ore and the best sunlight in the system at 440 kelvin. Venus gives sulphur and tungstotitanate at 737 and near-Earth gravity, which makes launching from it the most expensive.
Proxima b is the only destination with oxygen and Earth gravity, and also tier three: the end of the seventh epoch, not its middle. Summary: /if_planetary_processes.
industrial_frontier.quest.p7.planetary.t: Pick a planet against a specific production shortage
industrial_frontier.quest.p7.protected_z: The sixth epoch's reactor punished carelessness with the loss of a district. The seventh punishes with relationships: a strategic site has neighbours, and they can see what you are building.

Five requirements: the site stands outside housing and food districts, there is one known entrance, the backup line is sized for a full outage of the main one, feedstock and waste are stored apart and outside the shop, strategic materials are counted piece by piece.
A shortfall here is not a lost resource but an event. The full standing order is available via /if_strategic_zone.
Where such a thing may stand at all
Move the strategic site outside the housing boundary
The PUREX line — 55 recipes — pulls out of irradiated fuel whatever is still useful: plutonium, neptunium, technetium and leftover uranium. It runs on nitric acid and kerosene, flammable and corrosive at once.
So the line is separated from the power block, and a leak is contained before it reaches hot equipment. This is not caution in general but a specific property of the reagents.

Nuclear waste is a product, not rubbish. It carries a dose, it is counted by the single radiation model, and it lives in its own store. You cannot throw it into the world: it stays where it is thrown.
industrial_frontier.quest.p7.purex.subti: Nitric acid, kerosene and what is left over
industrial_frontier.quest.p7.purex.task: Set aside a waste store before the first reprocessing run
industrial_frontier.quest.p7.purex.title: Reprocessing and waste
industrial_frontier.quest.p7.radiation_m: The strategic domain ships its own radiation: chunk contamination, entity contamination, crater fallout and a separate pollution layer with its own Geiger counter and detector.

In this pack it is switched off. Dose, armour shielding and decontamination are handled by the sixth-epoch nuclear model — the very one you already used at the station. The instruments stay with it too: the second counter is removed.

The strategic domain's materials were added to its lists: plutonium, neptunium, polonium, uranium and waste carry a dose and are dangerous in your pocket, not only in a reactor. One scale, one remedy, the same rules.
Two dose models are not depth, they are a fault
Check a strategic material's dose with your own dosimeter
industrial_frontier.quest.p7.rbmk.desc.1: This is the second reactor type in the pack, and it is built differently from the civil one. The channel design — 62 assembly recipes — is put together by hand, column by column, and its behaviour depends on what you placed in each cell.
industrial_frontier.quest.p7.rbmk.desc.2: The key difference is speed. Rods are raised in steps with a pause to measure, and the remote console is installed before the first startup, not after the first lesson.
industrial_frontier.quest.p7.rbmk.desc.3: The stop button is physically reachable and duplicated outside the zone. After a shutdown decay heat remains: cooling keeps running even when the reaction has stopped.
industrial_frontier.quest.p7.rbmk.subtit: A reactor that runs away faster than you can walk
industrial_frontier.quest.p7.rbmk.title: The RBMK
industrial_frontier.quest.p7.return_flow: The pack's rule about mass components applies here too: a planetary material counts as part of the economy only when its return runs without you on every trip.

Four steps. The first trip is manual — it exists to learn the volume, not to become the norm. Second: mined material goes into a buffer on the planet, not into your inventory. Third: a regular run with automatic loading and a saved return point. Fourth: on Earth planetary feedstock enters the common store under the same rules as terrestrial.
While the return is manual, planetary feedstock enters no mandatory recipe. Space is not allowed to become the dullest mine in the game.
While it is manual, the planet is not settled
Make planetary return regular without manual loading
industrial_frontier.quest.p7.rocket_elec: The rocket does not choose where to fly. You do, and the choice is written to an identification chip before launch. Without a valid chip there is no launch — that is the hardware's requirement, not a convention.
The return point goes on the same chip. A rocket that left without a saved pad comes back somewhere other than where it started, and you find that out at the worst possible moment.

The scanner and telemetry check the assembled stage before ignition: tier of the parts, fuel volume and match to the destination. Everything that can be learned on the ground is learned on the ground.
industrial_frontier.quest.p7.rocket_fuel: Rocket fuel is not "combustibles in general". It is a distinct chemical product, and you cannot fill a stage with diesel: it has its own fluid, its own storage and its own throughput, which sets launch frequency far more than tank size does.
The oxidiser is liquefied oxygen. In vacuum there is nothing to burn with, so the cryogenic line is mandatory, not convenient. It is also what makes a spaceport a production site rather than a pad.
Boiled-off oxygen returns to the atmosphere and is harmless in that sense. The loss here is energetic: liquefying it again costs full price.
industrial_frontier.quest.p7.rocket_mate: A rocket starts not with an engine but with materials nothing has required so far. Polyimide, para-aramid, fibreglass and light alloys are a class, not a single item.

A composite does not substitute for steel of the same weight: it does what steel cannot — hold skin heating and not conduct that heat inward. The reverse substitution fails too: you will not make a load-bearing frame out of fabric.
All of it is synthesised from fourth-epoch petrochemistry. Space brings no new chemistry — it presents the bill for the chemistry you already built.
industrial_frontier.quest.p7.sealing_bas: The habitable loop closes completely, entry through an airlock. One unsealed cell in the ceiling vents the whole volume: sealing here is not a bonus but a condition. It is checked along the boundary, not by area.
Solar power depends on the planet and is known in advance: Mercury gives twice Earth's, Venus half. Design for the worst case, not the average.
On hot planets the problem is not collecting heat but rejecting it; on cold ones the opposite. The same base blueprint does not work in both. Full requirements: /if_offworld_base.
Sealing is checked along the boundary
industrial_frontier.quest.p7.spaceport.d: The spaceport is a contract of the same class as the city nuclear plant. Six requirements: a launch table with an exclusion zone, a fuel node, an oxygen line buffered for a full flight, a stage assembly shop, a power feed with reserve, and a control point holding the saved return position.

The contract is not issued while the launch table stands in a housing district or while fuel is carried by the bucket. A spaceport without an exclusion zone and without a line is not a spaceport, it is a bonfire.
The reward is not an item: the city gains a space port, and orbit and planets become part of its logistics. Contract details: /if_spaceport_contract.
industrial_frontier.quest.p7.spaceport.s: A city megaproject, not a pad
industrial_frontier.quest.p7.strategic_c: The charge was kept deliberately. Without it this domain has no role of its own beside civil nuclear power, and the seventh epoch becomes a second sixth.

Four rules come with it. The charge is not a shortcut: clearing terrain, mining and levelling a faction base instead of running an operation are forbidden — they cancel the negotiation window and the recovery path that every operation has.

Factions never hand it over, not as loot, not as trade, not as a reward. Using it is seen by all six at once, not only by the target. And the pack's general rule holds here too: the response is reversible, your base is not lost forever. Full list: /if_strategic_rules.

This also explains what you will not find in this mod. Its firearms, armour, ammunition and the benches for them are not craftable here: that was a second weapon system beside the one already chosen, and a cheaper one — a plain crafting table against the second-epoch steel bench. Small arms stay with their owner, artillery with its own. The charge is not a sidearm and replaces neither.
The one thing that exists nowhere else
Read the rules of use before the charge is assembled
industrial_frontier.quest.p7.suit_oxygen: Oxygen exists twice in this pack and comes from one line: as the engine's oxidiser and as a human's air. Same gas, same production — you cannot save on the buffer for either.
The suit needs the full set and a reserve. Upgrades go on before the flight: heat shielding for Venus and Mercury, insulation for the Moon. On arrival there will be neither time nor means.
The oxygen spreader holds a habitable volume and needs power. A reserve against supply failure is mandatory: repairing the line in a suit with no oxygen is already too late.
industrial_frontier.quest.p8.accelerator: The sixth epoch deferred these installations "until their own epochs". The epoch has come. The linear accelerator drives particles, the ring does the same in a circle and harder, the diverter steers the beam aside.
The point of the whole branch is that it yields substances no furnace and no reactor can. It is not a faster way to get the known — it is the only way to get the unknown.
The complex needs space, power and precise assembly. Half-built it does not work at all: there is no intermediate result here.
What no furnace and no reactor will make
industrial_frontier.quest.p8.diagnosis.d: A distributed factory has a new failure mode: it breaks quietly. A shop on another planet stopped a week ago, and you learn about it when Earth runs out of feedstock.
Hence the rule: a buffer on every leg, sized for the time in which you will certainly notice. Not for production volume — for your inattention.
Second rule: every chain needs an end you can see. One store that tells you whether the whole network is running.
industrial_frontier.quest.p8.diagnosis.s: Find out before the store runs dry
industrial_frontier.quest.p8.diagnosis.t: Put a buffer on every leg of the network
industrial_frontier.quest.p8.elevator.de: Every launch costs fuel. The elevator costs once — and after that the surface-to-orbit channel works with no rocket at all.
It is built like a megaproject and pays back only under constant traffic. If you go up once a week, flying is cheaper.
But under constant traffic it changes the economics of the whole programme: what used to be "too heavy to lift" becomes ordinary cargo.
industrial_frontier.quest.p8.elevator.su: Build once so you stop paying for the climb
industrial_frontier.quest.p8.elevator.ta: Decide whether your traffic justifies an elevator
industrial_frontier.quest.p8.flow.desc.1: The first run is always manual — it exists to learn the volume. The second must not be: loading, flight and unloading happen on schedule and without your presence.
industrial_frontier.quest.p8.flow.desc.2: The test is simple. Leave for an in-game week and come back. If the stores at both ends are exactly as you left them, there is no network — there is a route you operate by hand.
industrial_frontier.quest.p8.flow.desc.3: A buffer goes on every leg. Not for reserve but for diagnosis: while the buffer fills, you can see that something further along has stopped.
industrial_frontier.quest.p8.flow.subtit: A run that does not wait for you to show up
industrial_frontier.quest.p8.flow.title: Flow without you
industrial_frontier.quest.p8.fusion_spli: Fusion in this pack has two owners and they do not compete. The GregTech fusion reactor is a machine tool: it yields materials that exist nowhere else, and it works as part of a production line.

The HBM laser installation is a power plant. Dozens of blocks laid out to a blueprint, its own plasma forge for the parts and superconductors at the core. This is the main power source of the finale and the largest structure in the pack.
There is deliberately no third fusion: it would mean walking the same path a third time. You will not find NuclearCraft's fusion branch in game, and that is a decision, not an omission.
One makes materials, the other makes power
Choose where to start: materials or power
The seventh epoch answered "how do I get there". The eighth answers a different question: "why come back". The planets are open and each one is good at something — but while they live apart, all of it stays a collection of places you have visited.
A network turns them into one factory. Each planet does what only it can and sends the result onward by itself. Your work here is not to fly but to design so that flying is no longer needed.
The other half of the epoch is overhead. Orbit stops being transit and starts providing services: finding ore from above, running navigation, beaming power down.
industrial_frontier.quest.p8.intro.subti: Nowhere left to fly — time to connect
industrial_frontier.quest.p8.intro.task: Understand how a network differs from a set of bases
industrial_frontier.quest.p8.intro.title: The eighth epoch
industrial_frontier.quest.p8.navigation_: Routes stop being a note written to a chip before every launch. The constellation knows where things are, and the rocket takes its course by itself.
The key word is constellation. One satellite gives one point and no navigation; a network begins where there are enough of them to cover the whole route.
This is what turns interplanetary runs from an event into a routine. Which is exactly right: routine is what machinery is for.
industrial_frontier.quest.p8.plasma_forg: Everything the laser installation is built from is made here. The forge itself costs superconducting wire and quantum circuits — meaning you can only reach it through your own superconductor chain.
The pack puts no separate lock on it: the mod already made it late through its own materials. Same case as the space stack last epoch — where a ladder exists, you do not build a second one.
After this comes construction to a blueprint: vessel, laser ports, capacitors, turbochargers. A half-built installation gives nothing.
The door to the largest structure in the pack
An orbital station collects power and beams it down to a receiver. Useful where sunlight is weak, the atmosphere is hostile and there is no room for a plant.
Transmission losses are always there, and that is an honest price: you pay a percentage for not having to put the plant on the surface.
The vulnerability is honest too. The beam works while the station works. A receiver without a station is just a block.
A power plant where there is nowhere to build one
Renewables cover the base load, the reactor covers peaks and nights. The reverse means a reactor that is throttled up and down, which is the worst way to use one.
Solar output depends on the planet and is known in advance. On Mercury a panel pays back twice as fast as on Earth, on Venus twice as slowly. Identical solar farms on different planets do not exist.
Storage is mandatory. Renewables without storage are not power generation but weather, and capacity is sized for the longest pause, not the average one.
Renewables beside the reactor, not instead of it
Cover the base load with a renewable line
industrial_frontier.quest.p8.specialisat: The Moon gives a cheap launch: its gravity is six times weaker than Earth's, and lifting from there costs incomparably less. Mars is the richest planet of the programme. Mercury has the best sunlight in the system. Venus offers sulphur chemistry at a temperature that kills anything unprotected.
A planet joins the network only for what Earth does not have. Hauling iron from Mars while iron lies underfoot is not scale, it is a planning error.
Hence a simple test: if removing a planet from the chain breaks nothing, that planet does not belong in the chain.
Hauling the ordinary is a sign of error
industrial_frontier.quest.p8.survey_sate: Until now deposits were found on foot and by drill. A satellite sees them from above, and the difference is not convenience but an order of magnitude: a planet is surveyed in a single pass.
The price is the satellite, its launch and its power. On a planet you work daily it pays back immediately. On a planet you visit once a month it never will.
This is the first item of the epoch that produces nothing. It produces knowledge — and from here there will be more of those.
industrial_frontier.quest.p8.target_cham: The target chamber takes the accelerated beam and turns it into matter. The collision chamber brings two beams head-on — costlier, harder, and it yields what a single target cannot.
The terminal shows what is happening inside. Without it the complex runs blind, and a wrong setting shows up only as an absent result.
This is the most laboratory-like part of the pack: precision matters more than volume, and one correctly tuned complex beats three assembled carelessly.
Build the target chamber and the terminal
industrial_frontier.quest.p9.closed_loop: By now you have everything needed for production to stop consuming the non-renewable: power from a star, materials from planets, water and air in a closed loop, waste returning to the cycle.
This is the sustainable civilisation from the pack's definition of done. Not one expensive item but a chain with no point where something runs out for good.
Checking it is simple: find the place in your production where a resource comes from the world and never returns. If no such place is left, you are finished.
A chain that does not end
Find the last non-renewable point in your production
industrial_frontier.quest.p9.colony_indu: Life support is half the job. The other half is that the colony can reproduce what it is built from: replace what breaks, extend what stands, without waiting for a ship.
Its own power is mandatory and must not depend on Earth's grid. Proxima is another star system; no beam reaches that far.
This is the pack's hardest exam: to pass it you must rebuild on an alien planet nearly the whole chain you spent eight epochs building on Earth.
Its own production, its own power
Set up local production and power
industrial_frontier.quest.p9.colony_life: Proxima b is the only destination with oxygen and Earth-like gravity. That makes it liveable and, at the same time, the most deceptive target: it looks like you could just move in.

A colony counts as a colony when air, water and food are produced on site. A one-off delivery of equipment, yes. Regular food deliveries, no: that is not a colony but a warehouse with people at the far end of a route.
The test is the same as for the network: stop flying there for an in-game month. A colony that survives that has happened.
A settlement on supply is a warehouse with people
Close the colony's life support on site
The colony breathes on its own
The pack does not end with an item. No expensive ingot and no rare machine counts as a finale — you can obtain one and forget it, and a civilisation is not tested that way.

There are two finales and they test different things. The Dyson swarm is about scale: it cannot be built alone and cannot be abandoned, it demands flow and maintenance. The colony on Proxima b is about autonomy: it must survive when Earth stops sending ships.
You may build both, either one, or neither. These are two different finales, not two halves of one, and neither closes the other off.
industrial_frontier.quest.p9.intro.subti: The finale tests a civilisation, not a chest
industrial_frontier.quest.p9.intro.title: The ninth epoch
industrial_frontier.quest.p9.quantum.des: The quantum transformer does what the whole accelerator complex was built for: it turns energy into matter. It costs more than anything else in the branch and unlocks last.
Its point is that from now on power becomes feedstock. Anything you lack can be made — if you have the means to pay.
Which is exactly why it sits in the ninth epoch and not earlier: before the sphere or the colony there is nothing to pay with.
industrial_frontier.quest.p9.quantum.sub: The last machine of the accelerator branch
A megaproject cannot be taken: it is too large to carry off and too visible to hide. So politics grows around it rather than robbery, and the factions ask the question outright.

Sole ownership gives maximum return and maximum attention. A consortium trades part of the return for a quiet rear. Open access splits everything six ways but ends operations against the site. Guardianship hands control to one faction and leaves you a veto.
No option closes off game content and none counts as correct. The resolution changes how the region lives — and it is the pack's last decision. Full list: /if_endgame_resolutions.
Four answers, none of them wrong
A Dyson swarm is not a structure but a flow. Swarm satellites are needed by the hundred, and making them one at a time is pointless: by the time you hand-build the tenth, the first is obsolete.
So the first step is not a satellite but the line that produces them. Feedstock, assembly, launch: three sections, each of which must run without you.
A manual launch is allowed exactly once — the one where you check that the scheme works at all.
The swarm starts with a line
industrial_frontier.quest.p9.swarm_upkee: A finished sphere is not a monument. It wears out and needs maintenance, and abandoned it decays. This is the only structure in the pack that punishes you for forgetting about it.
So alongside the production line you need a repair line. And a reserve for when the swarm dips: a city fed only by the sphere goes dark with it.
That is the price of the largest power source in the game. It is a fair one: unlimited power without obligations is not a finale, it is a cheat mode.
Set up swarm maintenance and a reserve against dips
industrial_frontier.quest.passports.acce:
§6What the tag means§r
`industrial_frontier:materials/iron_nuggets` points to the accepted `forge:nuggets/iron` category. Valid suppliers can feed one process without being selected by appearance or namespace.

§6What it does not mean§r
The tag creates no recipe, changes no yield, upgrades no purity, and never approves a specialised state. Input compatibility and free conversion are separate decisions.

§6Your check§r
Keep one iron nugget in your main inventory until the task updates. The handbook checks the category and takes nothing.

§6If it fails§r
Confirm that the item is a real iron nugget rather than a decorative part. Then record the JEI ID; a legitimate form can be added only after its material balance is verified.
A pack tag states a physical compatibility rule
Any 1 iron nugget in the pack tag
industrial_frontier.quest.passports.anat:
§6Origin and epoch§r
The record begins with world-generation ownership, deposit or dimension, first honest access, and renewability. Trade and loot cannot be the only mandatory source without a deterministic alternative.

§6Representations and purity§r
Every form names a concrete ID or compatibility tag, its purpose, and a purity class. A common plate may be shared; a reagent, fuel, or irradiated state keeps its identity.

§6Process owners§r
Extraction, crushing, separation, smelting, reaction, and final assembly may belong to different domains. Each hand-off must be justified by scale, temperature, pressure, precision, safety, or logistics.

§6Consumers and residues§r
A required product has a useful downstream consumer. Every compulsory by-product receives recycling, storage, or safe automated disposal before demand becomes industrial.

§6Anti-grind§r
The passport records manual batches, repeated actions, waiting, RNG, and the first automation route. A lesson normally uses 1–3 batches; machinery arrives before the same action must be repeated more than 6–8 times.
Origin, forms, purity, processes, consumers, waste, and automation
industrial_frontier.quest.passports.bypa:
§6Step 1 — access§r
Compare machine epoch, tools, power, heat, and prerequisite components. An early interface must not accept late feedstock and emit a future-epoch result.

§6Step 2 — material balance§r
Count the main output, chances, by-products, containers, and returned catalysts. A shorter chain must not quietly multiply metal or purify it without residues.

§6Step 3 — the full cycle§r
Follow the route forward and backward across every mod. If the loop restores its input and leaves a profit, it is a duplication exploit even when each individual arrow looks plausible.

§6Step 4 — domain value§r
Ask whether the intended industry still has a reason to exist. A cheaper machine may trade purity, scale, or efficiency; unrestricted replacement is not a meaningful domain.

§6How to report it§r
Provide the input ID, every recipe ID in the route, outputs, and available epoch. Do not jump straight to removing a whole mod: a narrow correction can preserve the unique mechanic and eliminate only the bypass.
A faster route is valid only when it preserves the epoch and the industrial role
industrial_frontier.quest.passports.crea:
§6Domain roles§r
GTCEu specialises in exact metallurgy and demanding purification. Create specialises in visible mechanical flow, material handling, and its own functional parts. Neither domain rules the entire pack.

§6The hand-off§r
A Create mixer combines andesite with an iron or zinc nugget accepted through a Forge tag. The ordinary metal may come from any approved route; andesite alloy remains a Create product.

§6Inspect it in JEI§r
Press R over andesite alloy. Review both metal inputs and the process category. The task accepts the output without forcing the iron route over the zinc route.

§6Why this contract works§r
One domain supplies a clear standard form, another performs a characteristic operation, and the result serves that second domain's machinery. No conversion loop or material profit appears.

§6The boundary§r
This example does not authorise Create to turn every raw ore directly into finished metal. Ore routes are judged separately by process ownership and total yield.
Standard metal enters a visible mechanical process with a distinct purpose
industrial_frontier.quest.passports.enti:
§6Material entity§r
“Iron” names the material and its shared physical accounting. It does not become the exclusive property of whichever mod supplied the icon.

§6Form§r
An ingot is convenient stock, a plate builds housings, dust meters reactions, and molten metal supports fluid processing. A form changes the valid operations but must never create extra matter by itself.

§6ID and tag§r
An ID selects one implementation, such as `minecraft:iron_ingot`. `industrial_frontier:materials/iron_ingots` describes the category approved by the pack. A recipe uses the tag only when the ingot's origin has no physical relevance.

§6Your check§r
Carry one ordinary iron ingot. It will not be consumed. If a valid ingot is rejected, report its exact ID so the input contract can be audited instead of forcing you to swap items blindly.
Iron remains iron, while ingots, dusts, and plates serve different jobs
Any 1 iron ingot in the pack tag
industrial_frontier.quest.passports.intr:
§6The definition§r
A passport is the pack contract for one substance or material. It binds origin, accepted forms, purity, process owners, consumers, waste, epoch, and automation point. It is design data, not another inventory item.

§6Why it is enforceable§r
When two mods provide similar dusts or ingots, the passport says whether they are genuinely equivalent. When machines overlap, it records the difference in scale, precision, operating conditions, or cost. An unexplained duplicate is an integration defect.

§6How it helps you§r
JEI answers which recipe exists; the handbook explains why that route belongs here. A passport tells you which form may be accepted by a tag, which state must remain distinct, where the resource begins, and when manual work should give way to automation.
One source of truth instead of look-alike items and accidental recipes
I understand what a passport does
industrial_frontier.quest.passports.safe:
§6Where equivalence helps§r
An iron plate is often simply standard metal in a useful geometry. Recipes without a special tolerance or purity requirement may accept `industrial_frontier:materials/iron_plates`.

§6Accounting remains intact§r
The tag recognises a valid result but never doubles it or refunds more ingots than were spent. Machine, time, and cost still belong to the producing route.

§6Your check§r
Carry one accepted iron plate. In the currently installed stack, the category can include compatible Create and GTCEu forms; nothing is consumed.

§6Cycle audit§r
Before any reverse conversion is added, every output, by-product, and returned tool is counted. Even two apparently harmless 1:1 conversions can profit when another machine adds a bonus.
Several fair processes may supply one ordinary material form
Any 1 iron plate in the pack tag
industrial_frontier.quest.passports.sign:
§6What you can do§r
You can separate a material from its form and ID, read the passport fields, identify worldgen ownership, use an accepted tag, and audit a recipe route for shortcuts.

§6What this lesson does not do§r
It does not raise `tech_epoch`, award resources, or unlock future mods. The chapter is optional progression-wise, while its rules remain mandatory for every authored chain.

§6Next§r
The first playable slice will apply these contracts to prospecting, a mechanised settlement, industrial heat, steel, and LV. Every new form will have a clear source, purpose, and path to automation.
A cross-mod connection now needs a testable physical explanation
industrial_frontier.quest.passports.spec:
§6A standard form§r
A normal ingot or plate can be interchangeable when composition, mass, and use match. Tags make that ordinary compatibility painless.

§6A specialised state§r
High-purity reagents, reactor-grade material, irradiated samples, sealed food, and aerospace composites carry additional state. Flattening them into a generic dust would erase engineering and safety.

§6Purity class§r
Purity is an operating requirement rather than flavour text. It decides whether a material is suitable for electronics, controlled chemistry, or a hazardous facility, and which process certifies it.

§6A practical test§r
If substitution removes pressure, temperature, dimensional access, radiation protection, quality control, or an entire industrial branch, the forms are not equivalent even when they share one element.
Purity, hazard, and purpose can matter more than a shared element name
I understand the limit of equivalence
industrial_frontier.quest.passports.worl:
§6Why ownership matters§r
Parallel ores undermine prospecting, yields, and transport districts. Each substance receives one origin; other domains consume its approved forms through explicit contracts.

§6The current M2 baseline§r
Create ore generation is disabled, while GTCEu removes vanilla ore generation and supplies the installed vein system. This describes today's stack; it does not grant GTCEu automatic ownership of every future resource.

§6Future domains§r
An oil reservoir, planetary mineral, or reactor feedstock may receive another owner after its own audit. A new mod's worldgen stays off until the passport and configuration agree.

§6What to report§r
If two independently generated ores represent the same metal, or one source bypasses the approved processing route, preserve both block IDs and the dimension. That is a worldgen conflict, not a reason to merge outputs without analysis.
A resource should not spawn through several unrelated deposit systems
industrial_frontier.quest.settlement.bui: The builder erects every other building. Until you have one, the colony is a town hall and nothing more.
They work on request: you pick a blueprint and a spot, they ask for materials and build. You will have to supply those materials — a colony creates nothing from thin air, and that is the point.
Hence the classic day-one mistake: ordering five buildings at once. There is one builder, the queue is long, and your materials get locked into everything simultaneously. Build one at a time.
industrial_frontier.quest.settlement.gua: Barracks give the colony its own guards. They patrol the territory and fight whoever comes to the settlement.

This ties straight into factions. Operations target you, but they happen in a world where your settlement stands, and civilians are not fighters. Guards decide whether an operation becomes a negotiation or a loss.
The reverse also holds: killing another faction's civilian costs you eighteen points of standing. Your guards can start a fight you did not want.
A settlement is something you can lose
industrial_frontier.quest.settlement.int: A colony is a separate system: you place a town hall, hire a builder, and from then on residents build, mine, cook and guard according to your plan.

This is not decoration here. The industry in this pack is described as urban: municipal contracts, rations, water and housing exist because somebody has to live in all of it. A colony gives that meaning.
Mind the price. Residents need food, housing and building time. This is not free labour but a trade: you feed the settlement, the settlement removes your drudgery.
People who work while you are away
Why the pack wants a living settlement
industrial_frontier.quest.settlement.sup: Every resident eats and needs a bed. No food and people leave or stop working; no housing and no new ones arrive.
This is where two parts of the pack meet. The food chains you build in the fourth epoch — fields, kitchen, rations — gain a permanent consumer. The urban ration stops being a line in a contract.
The rule is simple: field and kitchen first, hiring second. A colony that grows faster than its supply falls apart on its own.
A colony consumes as much as it works
Food, housing and things that run out
industrial_frontier.quest.settlement.tow: The town hall declares colony territory and acts as the control panel: residents, orders, statistics and settings all live in it.
Pick the spot once and seriously. Leave room around it for housing, fields, stores and workshops, with water nearby. Moving a colony later is expensive and tedious.
A practical tip: do not place the hall flush against your factory. Noise and smoke will not bother the residents, but somebody else's construction site in the middle of your workshop will bother you.
The first building defines all the rest
The town hall and the colony border
industrial_frontier.quest.start.bulk_che:
§6Purpose§r
A factory quickly outgrows one chest. This recipe demonstrates a pack rule: simple repeated components may be made in batches when the material balance is not discounted.

§6Material balance§r
One chest costs eight planks. Four chests cost 32 planks, or eight logs at the normal four-plank yield. The new recipe creates no wood; it only removes intermediate crafts.

§6Exact layout§r
Open a crafting table. Fill the eight outer slots with logs from the Recast tag and leave the centre empty. The output must be exactly four chests.

§6Sign of success§r
Take the four chests and keep them in your inventory until the task updates. The book does not consume them: it verifies the lesson instead of charging a tax.

§6If the recipe is absent§r
Press R on a chest and find `industrial_frontier:m1/bulk_chest_from_logs`. If it is missing, check the Paxi datapack and KubeJS errors in `logs/latest.log`. Do not use `/give`; that would hide the cause.

§6Why this does not skip progression§r
Five interface operations were removed, but cost, era, tools, and production capacity were not. Future batching appears only after the original process has been taught once.

§6The next principle§r
A batch removes micro-crafting but does not build a factory. The next step is continuous flow: input buffer, machine, output buffer, throughput control, and a clear failure state.
The anti-grind reference: fewer clicks, unchanged cost
industrial_frontier.quest.start.jei.desc:
§6Recipe§r
Hover an item and press the recipe key, §eR§r by default. JEI lists every allowed production route and the machine each route needs.

§6Uses§r
Hover the item and press §eU§r. This shows why a component should be kept and which later processes consume it. Check both directions before committing to mass production.

§6Search§r
Type part of a name into JEI. The §e@§r prefix filters by mod, such as `@create basin`; §e#§r searches tooltip and tag text. If a recipe is missing, clear the filters and consult Help before creating anything with commands.
industrial_frontier.quest.start.jei.subt: Your item navigator, not a substitute for an engineering explanation
industrial_frontier.quest.start.jei.task: I checked a recipe and its uses
industrial_frontier.quest.start.next.des:
§6What you verified§r
You learned the book's notation, used JEI, separated team progress from personal state, checked a material tag, and completed a batch recipe.

§6What comes next§r
The optional Material Passports chapter now explains the shared rules for substances, ores, energy, and processes. P0 can then teach prospecting, basic supply, and the first production district without hidden recipe islands.
industrial_frontier.quest.start.next.sub: The real P0 progression comes next
§6Links and shapes§r
A line between quests marks a dependency. A large gear is a core lesson or technology milestone. A diamond closes a small stage. Circles in the help chapter never gate progression.

§6Do not guess§r
If a condition is unclear, read the full quest and then the matching Help and Diagnostics card. A required action should never exist only in somebody else's video or wiki.
Lines show required order; help chapters remain optional
industrial_frontier.quest.start.team.des:
§6One industrial project§r
FTB Teams owns shared quest progress. In multiplayer, create one team and invite everyone before completing required quests. Do not split one base across parallel teams.

§6Keep states separate§r
A future technology epoch will belong to the industrial team, while reputation, affiliation, and personal story facts remain distinct. Scoreboards will be read-only mirrors, never the source of truth.
industrial_frontier.quest.start.team.sub: Quests belong to a team; personal decisions belong to a player
§6What this pack is§r
Recast is not a pile of independent mods. You will build one connected industry: extraction feeds metallurgy, chemistry supports power and cities, cities create demand, and space requires a stable home economy.

§6How difficulty works§r
The pack asks for engineering decisions, not endless manual repetition. A new process is taught through one to three manual batches and then leads toward automation. Meaningless mandatory repetition is a balance defect worth reporting.

§6How to learn§r
Read pages in order. Lessons state inputs, outputs, start conditions, signs of success, and common faults. JEI answers “where and from what”; this book explains “why, how to connect it, and what comes next”.
Chemistry, factories, cities, and space form one system
industrial_frontier.quest.start.wood_tag:
§6Why tags matter§r
When wood species does not change the physics of a process, a quest accepts a material category. You should not hunt oak merely because it was chosen as the icon.

§6What to do§r
Carry eight ordinary logs. Species may be mixed as long as every item belongs to `industrial_frontier:materials/wood_logs`.

§6If it does not complete§r
Remove stripped products, planks, and bark: they are not logs. Check the item in JEI. If a real log is rejected, report its exact ID so the tag can be fixed instead of forcing a different material.
A tag accepts a valid material instead of one arbitrary wood colour
Any 8 logs in the Recast tag
industrial_frontier.quest.storage.cables: Cable carries the link over distance: a connector at the far end attaches crates in another room to the shared store.
This solves a real layout problem. Dirty and noisy things — the smeltery, the ore pile, the acid barrels — are kept away from the workbench, yet you still need to see their contents.
The limit is honest: cable has length and each connector consumes it. Plan the warehouse ahead instead of trailing a wire across the base.
The store need not sit where you do
Run cable to a remote store
industrial_frontier.quest.storage.connec: The connector looks at everything placed against it and declares the lot a single store. Chests stay chests — they simply gain shared bookkeeping.
The rule is simple: containers must touch the connector or each other. Break the chain of contact and part of the warehouse drops out, which is the most common beginner mistake.
In this pack it costs steel plates rather than a couple of planks. It is already an industrial tool: it saves you hours, so it must not arrive before steel does.
One block turns neighbouring crates into a whole
industrial_frontier.quest.storage.crafti: The crafting terminal adds a workbench to the list: you can assemble without pulling materials out by hand. The time saved is enormous, which is exactly why it only opens in the third epoch.
The pack rule does not change: convenience arrives after the problem it solves has started to hurt. With three recipes you do not need it; with three hundred it saves your evening.
Do not confuse it with autocrafting. It still needs you to press the button.
industrial_frontier.quest.storage.handov: The ME network arrives in the fifth epoch, raising a fair question: what was all this for. The answer is that they solve different problems.

This system shows and hands over what sits in ordinary chests. An ME network keeps items in its own cells, feeds machines through channels and eventually assembles things itself, without you. One is order, the other is production.

In practice: bulk and scrap stay here, because this is cheap and expendable. What takes part in autocrafting moves to ME. Wireless access is deliberately reserved for ME — that is its privilege, not your reward for patience.
Why ME does not cancel what you built
Where storage ends and the network begins
By the end of the first epoch you will own twenty chests and no idea which one holds the cog you need. That is not sloppiness, it is arithmetic: the number of distinct items grows faster than memory does.
The pack treats this as a production problem, not a housekeeping one. Time spent searching is no different from machine downtime.

This chapter covers three steps of order: labelled crates, a shared list and, much later, a network that fetches things for you. Each step costs its own materials and opens when the previous one stops coping.
Chests run out before ideas do
The emitter fires a signal when the stored amount of an item drops below a set number. That turns the warehouse from a display case into a sensor.
This is where automation by need begins, as opposed to automation by schedule. A machine starts when the stock runs out and stays quiet when there is enough, instead of grinding forever just in case.
The same trick underpins all late logistics. Here it costs redstone and a circuit; in the fifth epoch the same principle will drive entire lines.
Level emitter: the store answers with a signal
industrial_frontier.quest.storage.termin: The terminal shows the contents of the entire linked store as one searchable list. Twenty chests collapse into a single input field.
This is the first step where storage starts working for you. Mind its boundary: the terminal shows and hands over, but it produces nothing and carries nothing.
Put it where you actually work, not where the chests stand. The point is to stop walking.
The terminal: one list for the whole store
industrial_frontier.quest.workshop.assem: After the fourth epoch GregTech progression starts repeating itself: the same motors, pumps and pistons, only pricier. The component assembly line turns that into one configured process.
You declare which component and which tier you need, and the line delivers it as a stream instead of a dozen separate machines.
It arrives late, deliberately. The point is not to skip component production but to avoid walking through it by hand for the tenth time.
A cure for the dullest part of the late game
industrial_frontier.quest.workshop.choic: The pack rule is that a process has one owner. These four domains do not break it, because each occupies its own niche rather than replaying somebody else's.

The practical test is what you already run. Spare steam — take the foundry. Need power where a wire is awkward — take pressure. Prefer designing over buying — take photolithography. Tired of stamping motors — install the assembly line.
An honest warning: each is a separate system with its own rules. Taking all four at once means mastering none.
None of the four is mandatory
industrial_frontier.quest.workshop.found: The steam foundry smelts on steam, where before you chose between a furnace and waiting for a blast setup. The separator pulls more out of dust than plain washing does.
The point is that the steam age gained its own processing. Previously the gap between 'burned it in a furnace' and 'built an industrial plant' was a chasm, and the second epoch was mostly waiting.
Both run on steam you already produce. This is not a new supply branch but a way to squeeze more out of the boiler you built.
The second epoch stopped being thin
industrial_frontier.quest.workshop.intro: The main line is Create, then GregTech. Alongside them stand four more production systems, and each does something the main line cannot.

The steam foundry and separator deepen the second epoch, which used to be thin. Pneumatics give pressure as a separate kind of energy. Photolithography turns microchips into a process rather than a recipe. The component assembly line removes the dullest part of the late game.
None of them is mandatory. All of them are about a task having more than one honest solution.
Four domains, each with its own niche
What else the pack ships beside the main line
industrial_frontier.quest.workshop.litho: In GregTech a circuit is an item with a recipe. Here it is designed: you draw the logic on a workbench, print a mask, expose a silicon wafer and get a die.
The key difference is the reject rate. Yield is not a hundred percent, which honestly reflects what electronics manufacturing is. A batch can go entirely to waste.

This does not duplicate GregTech, it answers the same question differently. There you buy circuits with production volume; here you buy them with design precision. Both roads lead to automation and teach different things.
industrial_frontier.quest.workshop.press: Pneumatics store energy in compressed air. A compressor builds pressure, tubes distribute it, machines spend it.
The difference from electricity is fundamental: pressure has a burst limit. Overfill it and it ruptures — not an abstract breakdown but an explosion with a shockwave. The gauge is not decoration.
In exchange you get dense wireless energy and machines found nowhere else: drones, advanced plastic processing, air-driven automation. A small domain, but a deep one.
A third kind of power beside rotation and current
Build a compressor and raise pressure

industrial_frontier.screen.guide.body:
# Recast

Recast is a technology-and-city-building pack about chemical chains, connected factories, living settlements and the road from a field expedition to an interplanetary civilization.

## How to play

Once you enter a world, open the FTB Quests engineering handbook. The main route leads through epochs P0–P9; specialist chapters explain machinery, substances, safety, architecture and logistics. JEI tells you the recipe. The handbook tells you why the process exists and where it belongs in your plant.

## One industrial system

Every process has one owner, every substance has one passport, and all progression answers to one value: `industrial_frontier:tech_epoch`. A by-product needs a consumer or a safe disposal route.

## Pace

Recast does not ask for stockpiles of parts merely to consume time. Scale becomes mandatory only after the line is understood and automation is available.

## Safety

Radiation, pressure, chemical hazards and faction operations must warn the player clearly before an irreversible consequence.
